name: What is the difference between a kitchen layout redesign and a standard remodel?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a kitchen layout redesign and a standard remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: A kitchen layout redesign alters the physical footprint and placement of major work zones, while a standard remodel typically updates surfaces within the existing floor plan. In a redesign, you might shift the sink, relocate the range, reconfigure cabinetry runs, or eliminate walls to expand usable floor space. A cosmetic remodel leaves plumbing, gas lines, and walls intact, focusing only on replacing cabinet fronts, countertops, and backsplashes. Choosing a redesign makes sense when traffic bottlenecks or awkward appliance placements make daily cooking frustrating, though it requires more planning for structural, electrical, and plumbing changes.
acceptedAnswer.description: A redesign reconfigures the physical footprint, walls, and appliance locations, while a standard remodel updates finishes like cabinets and counters within the existing layout.
